title: Phoenix: continuous workload-aware batch recommender and safe-apply pipeline
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a continuous batching recommendation engine (codename: Phoenix) that profiles workloads, emits per-workload batching/caching recommendations, and applies configuration changes via a staged, safety-first rollout. Phoenix combines lightweight sampling, drift detection, cost-SLO scoring, and KV-cache awareness to produce conservative starting settings and incremental adjustments. The goal is to reduce per-token cost for eligible workloads by at least 12% without violating latency SLOs or degrading quality. Implementation spans profiler agents, a heuristics engine, a decision layer with simulated ROI, and a guarded apply pipeline that supports shadow, canary, ramp, and automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler captures representative request signatures and KV-cache hit distribution for >= 80% of sampled production routes
Heuristics engine outputs stable recommendations (batch_size, target_latency_p95, prefix_cache_enabled) and stores them in recommendations store
Simulated apply shows expected cost delta and latency impact; cost reduction >= 12% for at least 30% of profiled workloads in staging

Safe-apply pipeline supports shadow apply, canary (1% -> 10% -> 50%), and automatic rollback on thresholds: latency p95 increase > +20ms, error-rate delta > +0.5%, automated quality regression flagged by evals
Dashboards created for recommendation coverage, applied vs. reverted configs, and cost-savings attribution
End-to-end integration tests and a manual runbook for incident responders are in docs
tasks: Design sampling policy and lightweight signature schema (lead: ENG)
Implement profiler as sidecar/agent and integrate with telemetry pipeline
Prototype heuristics engine: cost-SLO scoring and kv-awareness
Build simulation runner to estimate cost/latency impact from historical traces
Develop safe-apply pipeline with shadow, canary, ramp, rollback hooks
Add dashboards and alerts (Console + Grafana) for recommendation health
E2E testing and staging experiments across GPU families and model families
Write runbook and postmortem template for apply-related incidents

rollout_plan: Shadow apply for 48h on staging traffic (no cost impact) to validate KV behavior
Canary phase: 1% production traffic for 4h -> 10% for 12h -> 50% for 24h
If all checks pass, ramp to 100% over 4h
During canary/ramp, run targeted evals for semantic quality on a prompt set per route
Maintain 7-day comparison window for cost attribution and telemetry baselines
rollback_plan: - evaluation quality metric regression (ROUGE/EM/F1) beyond route-specific threshold
Manual rollback steps documented in runbook with links to PR and previous config snapshot
Post-rollback investigation checklist: capture traces, profiler snapshots, and simulation logs
risk_assessment: Medium risk: changes affect latency and cost. Main hazards are long-tail latency regressions for certain model families and hidden KV-cache interactions that reduce cache hit rates. Mitigations: conservative starting defaults, model-family opt-outs, shadow validation, and automatic rollback thresholds coupled with evals-based quality gating.
impact: Expected to reduce overall hosted per-token spend for targeted routes by ~12-20% after full rollout while preserving latency SLOs. Also increases visibility into cache usage and long-tail behaviors, enabling future quantization/re-routing recommendations.
